target.title: fix(whatsapp): serialize overlapping Web sends
target.body:
Closes #99049

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where overlapping WhatsApp Web replies, media, reactions, or queued outbound messages could put multiple raw Baileys `sendMessage` calls in flight on the same active socket. Bursty traffic then left send ordering and socket coordination to Baileys instead of OpenClaw enforcing one active send at a time.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change serializes `sendMessage` at the shared socket-operation timeout boundary. The FIFO is keyed by the raw Baileys socket, so short-lived adapters created by the monitor, send API, and QA driver share one owner without a redundant facade queue. Presence updates remain outside the FIFO. A timed-out send releases the queue so one stalled Baileys promise cannot wedge later work.

The live WhatsApp QA catalog also gains an opt-in direct-Gateway scenario that uses independent RPC clients to create real request overlap, then requires all five distinct messages to arrive through the native WhatsApp driver.

## User Impact

WhatsApp Web operators should see deterministic outbound scheduling under concurrent sends for the same account. No configuration change is required. The change does not alter account setup, inbound monitoring, retry policy, or presence-update concurrency.

## Evidence

- Baileys contract inspected directly at pinned `baileys@7.0.0-rc13`: `sendMessage` ultimately awaits `relayMessage` and does not provide caller-level FIFO coordination.
- Focused regression: separate adapters over one raw socket cannot overlap `sendMessage`; success and rejection both advance the FIFO.
- Timeout regression: a stalled raw send rejects at the existing operation bound and releases the next queued send.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/socket-timing.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/whatsapp/whatsapp-live.runtime.test.ts` — 3 files passed; 125 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox-through-Crabbox `tbx_01kwretra15s7kjqrwekt3aksq` — `check:changed` passed extension production/test typecheck, changed-file lint, guards, and runtime import cycles. [Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28731773470).
- Fresh structured autoreview found one QA proof flaw: the first scenario version used one serialized RPC client. Fixed by using independent clients; final autoreview clean with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Real-transport attempt reached the Convex broker and leased the dedicated WhatsApp pair, but failed before scenario execution because the pooled driver session was logged out. The redacted run reported `WhatsApp QA failed during driver session start`; no live-pass claim is made.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.

Exact reviewed head: `3eff3495ee28514837e7b9d4f283b7291c52969b`.
